claims.text: Artificial intelligence models face security and robustness challenges in practical applications.
Most current AI models are designed with a black-box structure that lacks sufficient explainability.
Generative large language models experience hallucinations and associated robustness issues.

evidence.description: Robustness remains a major barrier to widespread adoption and contributes significantly to perceived untrustworthiness.
The invisible nature of black-box structures limits behavioral predictability and increases instability in complex environments.
Generative LLMs face unique robustness issues including hallucinations that require dedicated mitigation strategies.

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Review
methodologies.description: Systematic review examining evaluation methods and lifecycle enhancement strategies for AI model robustness.

limitations.text: Existing AI models lack explainability due to black-box architectures, causing instability in unknown environments.

future_work.text: Addressing open questions in AI model robustness and developing enhanced mitigation strategies for LLM hallucinations.
